questions.stem: Which tool lets users manage AWS services through a web-based user interface?

options.rationale: The CLI is a command-line tool, not a web interface.
SDKs are libraries for calling AWS from code.
CloudFormation provisions resources from templates.
The Management Console is the browser-based interface for AWS.

questions.explanation: Ways to access AWS: the Management Console (web), the AWS CLI (command line), AWS SDKs (code) and infrastructure as code.

questions.stem: Which option lets developers call AWS services directly from application code written in languages such as Python or Java?

options.rationale: AWS SDKs provide language-specific libraries for AWS APIs.
The console is used interactively in a browser.
Direct Connect is a dedicated network connection.
Artifact provides compliance reports.

questions.explanation: SDKs wrap the AWS APIs so applications can use AWS services programmatically.

questions.stem: A system administrator wants to automate routine AWS tasks with scripts run from a terminal. Which tool fits best?

options.rationale: The console is interactive and not suited to scripting.
The AWS CLI controls AWS services from the command line and scripts.
WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops.
Marketplace is a software catalog.

questions.explanation: The AWS CLI is a unified tool for managing AWS services from a terminal and automating them through scripts.

options.text: Writing application code that runs on virtual servers
options.rationale: That is ordinary application development.

options.text: Storing application source code in Amazon S3 buckets
options.rationale: Where code is stored does not make it infrastructure as code.

options.text: Defining infrastructure in templates or code so it can be provisioned repeatably
options.rationale: Infrastructure as code treats infrastructure definitions like software: versioned, reviewed and repeatable.

options.text: Configuring each resource by hand in the AWS Management Console
options.rationale: Manual configuration is the opposite of infrastructure as code.

questions.explanation: AWS CloudFormation is AWS's infrastructure as code service.

questions.stem: A team must create identical development, test and production environments many times a year. Which approach is most suitable?

options.text: Click through the AWS Management Console for each environment
options.rationale: Manual steps are slow and error-prone for repeated work.

options.text: Copy settings from a spreadsheet by hand each time
options.rationale: Manual copying invites drift between environments.

options.text: Ask AWS Support to build each environment
options.rationale: AWS Support does not build customer environments.

options.text: Use infrastructure as code templates, such as AWS CloudFormation
options.rationale: Templates create the same environment every time, which suits repeatable processes.

questions.explanation: One-time operations can be done by hand; repeatable processes should be automated with infrastructure as code.

questions.stem: A company keeps some workloads in its own data center and connects them to workloads running on AWS. Which deployment model is this?

options.rationale: A hybrid deployment connects on-premises infrastructure with cloud resources.
An all-in cloud deployment runs everything in the cloud.
On-premises deployments run everything in the company's own data center.
Multi-Region describes where cloud workloads run, not the deployment model.

questions.explanation: The three deployment models are cloud, hybrid and on-premises (also called private cloud).

questions.stem: A startup runs every one of its applications on AWS and owns no data center. Which deployment model is this?

options.rationale: Hybrid mixes on-premises and cloud.
A cloud-based deployment runs all parts of the application in the cloud.
On-premises means running in the company's own data center.
Colocation is renting space in a third-party data center for your own hardware.

questions.explanation: Cloud deployments can be built entirely on cloud-native services or migrated from existing infrastructure.

questions.stem: Which option creates an encrypted connection between an on-premises network and an Amazon VPC over the public internet?

options.rationale: Direct Connect is a dedicated private connection that does not use the public internet.
CloudFront is a content delivery network.
Site-to-Site VPN creates encrypted IPsec tunnels over the internet.
Global Accelerator routes user traffic to applications over the AWS network.

questions.explanation: Connectivity options: the public internet, AWS VPN (encrypted over the internet) and AWS Direct Connect (dedicated private link).

questions.stem: A company needs a dedicated private network connection from its data center to AWS with consistent network performance. Which service should it use?

options.rationale: A VPN runs over the public internet, so performance can vary.
Route 53 is a DNS service.
CloudFront delivers content to end users.
Direct Connect provides a dedicated network connection that bypasses the public internet.

questions.explanation: Direct Connect is chosen for consistent performance, high bandwidth or keeping traffic off the internet.

questions.stem: Which TWO are ways to access and manage AWS services programmatically? (Choose TWO.)

options.rationale: WorkSpaces provides virtual desktops.
SDKs call AWS APIs from application code.
Marketplace is a software catalog.
The CLI sends API requests from a terminal or script.
Artifact provides compliance documents.

questions.explanation: Programmatic access means using AWS APIs, directly or through the CLI and SDKs.
